tasks.short: Enforce school rules in class and the workshop, talk with students who break them, record incidents and late arrivals, inform the mentor about repeated incidents, and look up school policy when unsure.

steps.what: Technical teacher enforces administration policies and rules governing students in class and the workshop
Technical teacher talks with students who break the rules
Technical teacher records incidents and late arrivals in the student system
Technical teacher e-mails the mentor about repeated incidents
Technical teacher looks up school policy when unsure

tasks.design: The student system ({OTHER}) has quick buttons for late arrival, missing safety gear and phone use, and repeated incidents show in the mentor's view, so the teacher e-mails only when context is needed. School policies sit on one searchable page. Enforcing rules and talking with students stay with the teacher; incident data are used for guidance, not ranking students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents were typed in free text and mentors informed by e-mail each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems offer quick incident entry and mentor views.
tasks.still_hard: Consistent enforcement depends on every teacher, not a system.
tasks.human_edge: Correcting a student without losing them for the rest of the lesson.

evidence.claim: Student systems can record incidents with quick buttons and show them to mentors.
Under the WMS, parents and pupils consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the school rules to the mentor informed; sanctions by the year head are outside.
Input contract: rules set by the school; incident types agreed with mentors; fallback is free text and e-mail.
Enforcing rules and talking with students do not change.

Recording incidents and late arrivals is a first record: s3 keeps 85, saving only typing the common types with quick buttons. The mentor reads repeated incidents in the same system, so no separate send is needed; s4 keeps 20 for e-mails that add context.
research_questions: Do mentors act on repeated incidents sooner?

incremental.description: Technical teacher corrects wrongly recorded incidents.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few incidents fit the quick buttons and mentors still expect e-mails, so s3 keeps 95 and s4 keeps 60 (6.2); high: the buttons and mentor view used as designed (11.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Encourage students in lessons, set stretch tasks, discuss next-year choices and follow-on programmes, look up programmes and open days, and write progress notes.

steps.what: Technical teacher encourages students to explore learning opportunities and to persevere with challenging tasks
Technical teacher sets stretch tasks for students who are ready
Technical teacher looks up follow-on programmes and open days
Technical teacher discusses next-year choices and follow-on programmes with students
Technical teacher writes progress notes

tasks.design: Stretch tasks come from the section's task bank with levels, so the teacher picks rather than writes. The school's guidance page lists follow-on programmes and open-day dates per trade, kept by the career counsellor. Progress notes use a short template in the student system ({OTHER}). Encouraging students and discussing their choices stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stretch tasks were written ad hoc and programme information searched each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Task banks with levels and school guidance pages are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Perseverance grows from relationships, not tasks.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a student to try once more after a failed weld.

reach.learn: Whether the guidance page is used.

evidence.claim: Task banks can hold practice tasks by level; school web pages can list follow-on programmes and open days.

assumptions: Boundary: from class work to progress notes; formal career guidance is outside.
Input contract: task bank kept by the section; guidance page kept by the career counsellor; fallback is ad hoc tasks and searching.
Encouraging and discussing do not change.
Progress notes are a first record: s5 keeps 85, saving only the layout and standard fields.
research_questions: Do more students take stretch tasks?

incremental.description: Technical teacher adds stretch tasks to the bank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few tasks in the bank fit and the guidance page is incomplete, so s2 keeps 90 and s4 keeps 80 (3.7); high: many students using the bank and the page (9.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the project or trip, agree the visit with the host, collect parents' consent, check the trip plan, book the bus, supervise students during the activity, and guide their reflection.

steps.what: Technical teacher plans class projects, field trips and visits by guest speakers
Technical teacher agrees the date and programme with the host company or speaker
Technical teacher prepares the consent request: a paper form today, a consent form in the parent app after the change
Technical teacher checks the consent request before it goes: date, programme, costs, transport and the students on the trip list
Technical teacher sends the checked consent request to the parents in the parent app
Parents sign the consent form: on paper today, in the parent app after the change
Technical teacher collects parents' consents and chases those who have not signed: paper forms today, from the app's list after the change
Technical teacher checks the final trip plan, the consents and the bus booking: date, times, number of students and pick-up point
Technical teacher books the bus with the transport company: by phone today, through the company's online form after the change
Technical teacher supervises students during the activity
Technical teacher guides students in learning from the activity

tasks.design: A trip checklist template in the document space ({DOCS}) covers insurance, supervision ratio and dietary needs. The teacher checks the consent request and sends it once in the school's parent app; parents sign there, and the app shows who has not yet signed. Once the teacher has checked the trip plan, consents and booking details, the teacher books the bus once through the transport company's online form. Agreeing the visit with the host, supervising and guiding reflection stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consent forms came back on paper and trips were arranged by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Parent apps take digital consent; transport companies take online bookings.
tasks.still_hard: Host companies change dates at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a company visit into a student's first idea of a career.

evidence.claim: School parent apps can collect digital consent from parents.
Under the WMS, parents consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from learning goals to learning reflected; the school's trip budget is outside.
Input contract: checklist set by the school; host contacts in the school's internship database; fallback is paper and phone.
Parents sign in the app (s4, share 1) in about the time a paper form took; priced as customer time.
Supervising and guiding do not change.
research_questions: Do fewer students miss trips for missing consent?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; chasing parents is part of s3 and parents' signing is shown in s4.

approvals.approved_version: The bus booking with date, times, number of students and pick-up point from the trip plan exactly as checked by the teacher in s5, sent once through the transport company's online form; any change needs a new check.

The consent request with date, programme, costs and transport exactly as checked by the teacher in s3b, sent once to the parents of the students on the trip list in the parent app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many parents keep to paper forms, so collecting consents keeps 70 (11.4); high: most parents sign in the app (13.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the student's record, invite parents, have parents choose a slot, meet parents, confer with colleagues, counselors and administrators, and record the agreements.

steps.what: Technical teacher reads the student's record before the meeting
Technical teacher invites parents to a meeting by phone
Parents agree a meeting time: by phone today, by choosing a slot in the parent app after the change
Technical teacher confers with parents to resolve the student's behavioral and academic problems
Technical teacher confers with other teachers, counselors and administrators in the case meeting
Technical teacher records the agreements in the student record

tasks.design: A mentor view in the student system ({OTHER}) shows results, absence, incidents and earlier agreements together. Parents choose a meeting slot in the parent app after a short invitation, instead of a round of phone calls. Agreements go into a template with actions and a follow-up date. Meeting parents and the case meeting stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information came from several screens and meetings were arranged by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems offer mentor views; parent apps offer slot choice.
tasks.still_hard: Some parents are hard to reach by any channel.
tasks.human_edge: Getting parents and school on the same side of the table.

reach.learn: Whether slot choice gets meetings planned sooner.

evidence.claim: Student systems can show results, absence and incidents in one mentor view; parent apps offer slot choice.
Under the WMS, parents and pupils consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's concern to the recorded agreements; formal care plans are outside.
Input contract: record data from the student system; slots opened in the parent app; fallback is phone.
Parents choose a slot in the app (s3, share 1) in about the time a phone call took; priced as customer time. s2 keeps 40 for the invitation and phoning parents who do not use the app.
Meetings with parents and the case meeting do not change.
Recording agreements is a first record: s6 keeps 85, saving only the layout and standard fields.
research_questions: Do meetings happen sooner after a concern?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; phoning parents without the app is part of s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many parents prefer the phone, so inviting keeps 80 (9.5); high: most parents on the app (13.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technical teacher keeps enforcing rules, encouraging students, supervising trips and meeting parents; free-text records, ad hoc searching, paper consent and phone rounds shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the parent app for consent and meetings
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time to bring the trade into the classroom.
